title: The first text message
hook: The first text message said Merry Christmas and was typed on a computer.
peek: In December 1992 an engineer in England sent the first text message to a mobile phone. It said Merry Christmas. He had to type it on a computer, and the man who received it had no way to text back.
lede: On 3 December 1992, Neil Papworth, a 22-year-old engineer working on Vodafone's network in England, sent the first SMS. It read "Merry Christmas" and went to Richard Jarvis, a Vodafone director, who was at a staff Christmas party with his phone. Papworth typed it on a computer, because no handset could yet write a text.

bullets.text: Jarvis received the message on an Orbitel 901, a phone that weighed about two kilograms. It could display a text but not send one, so the very first message never got a reply.

bullets.opening: The first phones that could text
bullets.text: Nokia's handsets were among the first to let people type and send texts, from 1993. Even then, texting between different networks took several more years to arrive.

The 160-character limit came from the German engineer Friedhelm Hillebrand. He typed sentences and questions on a typewriter and counted, and found that most short messages fit comfortably in that space.
